rules.title: NJ residential rental application fee cap ($50, CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent cannot charge more than $50 for an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental. The cap is adjusted annually for CPI, and violators face penalties, with the wrongly charged amount remitted to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
rules.effective_date_note: Approved 2026-01-20; takes effect first day of the fourth month following enactment = 2026-05-01.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, up to $750 second, up to $1,000 each subsequent; wrongly charged amount refunded to applicant from penalty.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties other than 1-2 family dwellings.

parsed.doc_summary: NJ P.L.2025, c.405 caps residential rental application fees at $50 (CPI-adjusted annually), exempts 1-2 family dwellings and non-landlord real estate licensees, sets penalties, and took effect 2026-05-01 (approved 2026-01-20).
